ap_physics_1-m01.stem: A ball is thrown straight up with a speed of $10\text{ m/s}$ from the edge of a cliff that is $15\text{ m}$ above the ground. The ball misses the cliff on the way down and lands on the ground below. Air resistance is negligible. What is the speed of the ball just before it lands?

options.why: On the way down the ball passes the launch point with speed $10\text{ m/s}$ downward, so $v^2=v_0^2+2gh=100+2(9.8)(15)$ and $v=19.8\text{ m/s}$.
Ignores the initial speed, using only the speed gained in falling the cliff height.
Subtracts the squares: $\sqrt{2gh-v_0^2}$.
Uses the initial speed only, assuming the ball returns to the launch speed at the ground.

ap_physics_1-m02.stem: A $1\text{ kg}$ block is held at rest against a rough vertical wall by a horizontal force $F$ that presses the block against the wall. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the wall is $0.4$. What is the minimum magnitude of $F$ that keeps the block from sliding down?

options.why: The wall supplies a normal force $N=F$, so the largest static friction is $\mu F$. Holding the block requires $\mu F=mg$, so $F=mg/\mu=24.5\text{ N}$.
Multiplies the weight by the coefficient of friction, $\mu mg$, instead of dividing.
Divides the weight by $\mu+1$, a mistaken combination.
Divides the mass by the coefficient of friction without multiplying by $g$.

ap_physics_1-m03.stem: A sign of mass $10\text{ kg}$ hangs at rest from two light ropes. The two ropes are attached to the same ceiling and each makes an angle of $40^\circ$ with the horizontal, on opposite sides of the sign. What is the magnitude of the tension in each rope?

options.why: The vertical components of the two tensions support the weight: $2T\sin\theta=mg$, so $T=mg/(2\sin\theta)=76.2\text{ N}$.
Divides the weight equally between the ropes, forgetting the angle: $mg/2$.
Reports the horizontal component of the tension instead of the tension.
Uses the full weight divided by the sine, treating one rope as carrying the whole load.

key_conditions.evidence: the stem states the sign is at rest and the ropes make equal angles

ap_physics_1-m04.stem: A U-shaped tube open at both ends contains water (density $1000\text{ kg/m}^3$). Oil of density $900\text{ kg/m}^3$ is poured into one arm until the oil column is $12\text{ cm}$ tall. The oil does not mix with the water. The liquids are at rest. How high is the water column above the oil-water interface in the other arm?

options.why: At the level of the interface the pressure is the same in both arms: $\rho_og h_o=\rho_wg h_w$, so $h_w=(900)(12)/1000=10.8\text{ cm}$.
Inverts the density ratio: $h_o\rho_w/\rho_o$.
Adds the two column heights.
Uses the difference of the densities, $h_o(\rho_w-\rho_o)/\rho_w$.

key_conditions.condition: the liquids are at rest and both arms are open to the atmosphere
key_conditions.evidence: the stem states the tube is open at both ends and the liquids are at rest

misconceptions.description: Inverts the density ratio: $h_o\rho_w/\rho_o$.

Uses the difference of the densities, $h_o(\rho_w-\rho_o)/\rho_w$.
